title: Securing Microservices in a Multi-Tenant E-commerce Platform
business: A multi-tenant e-commerce provider hosting various vendor storefronts on a shared Kubernetes cluster.
problem: The platform faces significant security risks due to lateral movement, where a compromised pod in one vendor's namespace could potentially access sensitive data or services in another vendor's namespace.
solution: Calico Network Policies provide granular, label-based traffic control that allows the platform to enforce a zero-trust architecture, ensuring that pods can only communicate with explicitly authorized services regardless of their physical location on the cluster.
steps: Install Calico Open Source on the Kubernetes cluster to enable the CNI and policy enforcement engine.
Define a GlobalNetworkPolicy to implement a default-deny posture for all inter-namespace traffic.
Apply specific NetworkPolicy resources using label selectors to whitelist traffic between authorized microservices.
Utilize Calico's staged policies to preview the impact of new security rules on existing traffic flows before final enforcement.
outcome: A hardened environment where inter-tenant traffic is strictly isolated, significantly reducing the blast radius of potential security breaches.
limitation: The primary limitation is the increased operational complexity of managing a large set of granular policies, which can lead to configuration drift; this can be checked by auditing policy logs and using the Calico flow visualization tools to identify orphaned or overly permissive rules.

diagram.title: Calico Policy Enforcement Flow
diagram.description: This diagram illustrates how Calico intercepts traffic between pods to enforce security policies based on labels.

code.content:
apiVersion: projectcalico.org/v3
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-frontend-to-backend
spec:
  selector: role == 'backend' # Target the backend pods
  ingress:
  - action: Allow
    source:
      selector: role == 'frontend' # Only allow traffic from frontend pods
code.explanation: This policy restricts backend access to only those pods labeled as frontend, preventing unauthorized access from other namespaces.
